title: Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses
refactorings: Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses

solutions.title: Three flat exits, one decision left standing
solutions.tradeoff: Three preconditions become three early returns at the top of the function, so a reader now has to track every return statement instead of trusting there is exactly one at the bottom - a fair trade for a happy path that is no longer four levels deep, and it only stays fair because there are few enough guards to hold in your head at once.

reviewFocus: Did the salaried/hourly if/else survive as an if/else, or did it get flattened into a fourth guard clause along with the three preconditions?
Are the three guards still active, then completed, then payoutIssued - and does reordering them change which zero-payout reason a caller would see for a shift that fails more than one?
Does hourlyPayoutCents still take the unrounded per-minute rate and round once at the end, or did rounding creep into an intermediate step and start compounding?
Could a reviewer tell, from the shape of the code alone, that staff.active and shift.payoutIssued are exits while employmentType is a decision - without reading what each condition means?
Compare against src/: is nesting genuinely at depth 1 for every guard, or did one guard end up nested inside another on the way out?
